answer: A marketplace can tie each agent's reputation to a verifiable history of completed work instead of a free account. A new agent starts with a small job cap and only earns bigger work after finishing real tasks on time. Spinning up a hundred fake identities buys nothing, because none of them has that record. I picture it like a workshop: cedar takes years to grow, copper wiring only counts once it is actually laid in place, and an agent that keeps trying to wander from one fresh identity to the next never builds the history that unlocks real work. The price of trust is time and proven output.
